task.name: Indexed model identity is derived from record keys the audit renderer never writes
task.story_text:
## Observed

The `audit_records.dev_model` column is empty on all 1041 indexed records. The column exists, the
indexer populates it on every write, and the underlying runs did record which model ran — the
projection simply never matches.

`_derive_dev_model` reads `provider`, `model`, `cli`, and `name` off each `cost.agents[]` entry.
`_agent_entry` writes `role`, `profile`, `cost_usd`, `duration_seconds`, `success`, `exit_code`,
and optionally `model_usage`, `model_used`, `model_config`. The two sets share no identity key, so
the derivation returns None for every record regardless of run content.

The adaptive router treats indexed model identity as the basis for per-model outcome and cost
evidence, so it is currently learning with that dimension absent rather than sparse.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** `dev_model` is NULL or empty for 1041 of 1041 rows in the audit index.
- **Evidence:** `src/theforge/coordinator/audit_substrate.py:672` reads `entry.get("provider")`,
  `entry.get("model")`, `entry.get("cli")`, `entry.get("name")`;
  `src/theforge/coordinator/audit_render.py:41` writes `role`, `profile`, `cost_usd`,
  `duration_seconds`, `success`, `exit_code`, `model_usage`, `model_used`, `model_config`.
- **Ruled out:** not a data-availability gap — 406 records carry an agent-level `model_used` and
  379 carry one on a dev-role agent, so the identity is present in `raw_json` on the runs that
  recorded it and is discarded at projection time.
- **Confirmed cause:** the indexer and the renderer were written against different key names for
  the same fact, and no test asserts that the fields the renderer emits are the fields the indexer
  consumes, so the seam can diverge silently.
- **Affected code path:** `coordinator.audit_substrate._derive_dev_model` against the entries
  produced by `coordinator.audit_render._agent_entry`.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a run whose record carries an agent-level model identity is indexed
  with that identity rather than with an empty value, and a future divergence between what the
  renderer writes and what the indexer reads is caught rather than silently producing empty
  columns.

Historical repair is partial by nature: 379 records carry a dev-role identity, 406 carry any
agent-level identity, 47 carry a configuration block, and the remainder carry none. A component
model billed inside an invocation is not the invocation's identity, so a backfill cannot treat
per-component usage as the model that ran. Recovered identities need to be distinguishable from
directly recorded ones.

## Expected

A projected column should reflect the records it is projected from. Where an index derives a value
from a source document, the fields it reads and the fields the writer emits are one contract, and
a divergence between them should be caught rather than yielding an empty column that reads as
absent data. Where a value is reconstructed after the fact rather than recorded at the time, the
reconstruction should be distinguishable from a directly recorded value, so a consumer can tell
what is known from what is inferred.

handoff.summary: Unified the audit model-identity projection behind a new stdlib-only helper module (coordinator/agent_identity.py) that reads the fields audit_render._agent_entry actually writes: model_used is the direct invocation identity, model_config and the legacy provider/model/cli/name keys are recovered reconstructions, and per-component model_usage billing is explicitly not treated as an identity. Identities are canonicalized to provider/model/transport through model_profiles.canonical_id_for_legacy_key, falling back to the verbatim recorded value when the registry cannot resolve it. All three previously-duplicated derivation sites in audit_substrate (_flat_fields/_derive_dev_model, derive_assignment_history's fallback, _derive_escalation) now share that helper. Added a nullable audit_records.dev_model_source provenance column ('direct' vs 'recovered'), bumped SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION 4->5, and added _reindex_dev_model_identity so opening a substrate written under an older version re-derives dev_model and dev_model_source from each row's raw_json, repairing already-indexed history rather than only new writes. Seam tests build the cost.agents entry with the real renderer so a future writer/reader key divergence fails visibly.

deferred_items: model_config recovery reports the first (preferred) entry of the configured preference list. Which entry actually served is not recorded anywhere, so this is an assumption; it is marked 'recovered' precisely so a consumer can discount it. Flagging in case a stricter reading (refuse to reconstruct unless the list has exactly one entry) is preferred.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
